column1: # Whether each external app's `make test-php-unit` is expected to pass in the
# monorepo's PR gate, and if not, why.
#   php_unit=yes           runs and passes from a plain checkout. 21 apps.
#   php_unit=none          the app has no PHP unit tests to run. 2 apps.
#   php_unit=broken        it has a test-php-unit target that cannot work. 1 app.
#   php_unit=needs-service it needs a server the PR gate does not start
#                          (clamav, an FTP server, Dropbox credentials, S3,
# Measured, not guessed: every row is the result of running the target in the
# build image against one installed server (work/logs/appsweep.log), 2277 tests
# The upstream_gate column is the falsifiable half. It records which workflow --
# recovered from each app's own .github/ before this repo removed it -- actually
# ran php-unit for that app before the merge. Note what it says: of the 8 apps
# that do not pass here, 6 had NO php-unit job at all in their own repository.
# Their suites were not broken by the monorepo; the monorepo is what noticed.
# drawio is the clearest case -- its Makefile asks phpunit for a testsuite named
# `openidconnect-unit` and the app has no phpunit.xml, so the target has never
# been able to run, and nothing was watching.
# Consumed by .github/workflows/app-unit.yml, which skips the non-yes rows and
# says so in the run summary rather than silently reporting green.
